White Sox hit six home runs in 22-4 victory to take 1-0 lead in best-of-five series

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:27
Instaread

Collegeville opened the Perkiomen Valley Twilight League championship series with an offensive outburst Monday night, hitting six home runs in a 22-4 victory over Lansdale at Weaver Field in Memorial Park.

Liam Greenberg put the second-seeded White Sox ahead for good with a two-run homer in the second inning, per gameplay coverage from The Times Herald. Collegeville broke the game open with five runs in the third, highlighted by Cody Clarke’s two-run homer and consecutive RBI singles from Greenberg, Eric Berman and Kyle Feaster. Jordan Siket added a two-run shot in the fourth to extend the lead to 9-1.

Lansdale cut the deficit to 9-4 in the bottom of the fourth behind a sacrifice fly from Rob Zinsmeister and a two-run single by Matt Cavagnaro. Collegeville immediately answered with three runs in the fifth before sending its first nine batters across the plate during a nine-run sixth inning. Trevor Hansen delivered the biggest blow with a grand slam, and Collin Jensen completed the scoring with a solo homer in the seventh.

Greenberg went 4-for-5 with two home runs, four RBIs and three runs scored. Clarke, Siket and Hansen also drove in four runs apiece. Jackson Malouf earned the win after allowing four runs over five innings, while Chase Fisher pitched two hitless innings in relief. Collegeville leads the best-of-five championship series, 1-0.
